Is it "robust"? Yes: p < 0.05.
NASA and the US call the study's n = 128 cases "reliable".
R&D needs long-term evidence (Smith et al., 2021).
Table 2.1 lists costs and/or gains. Figure 3 shows them.
Figure 3 compares the UK and US samples (Lee et al., 2022). The report calls the trend "stable"; e.g., both groups improved by 12.8%.
The methods cover three stages: recruitment, review, and analysis. Participants read the same instructions, and the team recorded each response [24].
The R&D review found a 36.2% reduction in waste (Jones et al., 2023). Could this reflect a change in demand? The authors tested that explanation before accepting the result.
Table 4.2 reports the mean, range, and sample size: n = 256, p < 0.01. Its notes distinguish short-term variation from a sustained change; the difference matters for planning.
A second NASA study assessed water quality [36]. It found that 18.4% of samples exceeded the threshold, while the control group remained within the expected range.
The analysis follows the same sequence in each region: collect evidence, compare estimates, and report uncertainty. A missing value is marked as unavailable rather than treated as zero (Brown et al., 2020).
Figure 5 shows the distribution before and after the policy change. The central estimate rose from 21.6% to 34.9%, but the intervals overlap. The report therefore describes the evidence as "promising, with limits".
The review considers cost and/or reliability when comparing options. Long-term maintenance may outweigh an initial saving; the discussion separates those effects and states the assumptions [48].
The final model includes age, location, and prior experience. Table 6.1 gives the adjusted estimates (Smith et al., 2024), with n = 512 and p < 0.05 for the main comparison.
These findings support further evaluation rather than an immediate change in policy. What additional evidence would resolve the uncertainty? A larger sample and an independent replication would strengthen the case.
The conclusion returns to the research question and weighs the evidence fairly. Future R&D should test the mechanism in other settings, publish the full methods, and explain any departures from the plan [60].
